Findings.title: Configuration-key aliases escape temporary-instance isolation
Findings.defect: The inherited-environment scrub and start check recognize raw prefixes such as QBrainAi__ and Mcp__, but not equivalent colon-delimited or mixed colon/double-underscore configuration keys. An inherited QBrainAi:Database:Sqlite:ConnectionString survives the scrub and is ignored by the ownership check beside the owned QBrainAi__Database__Sqlite__ConnectionString. The .NET environment provider normalizes double underscores to colons and assigns normalized keys in enumeration order. If the inherited alias is assigned last, it supplies the database connection string. The configured connection string is used before the owned data-source fallback. Consequently the claimed refusal before access to an outside database is not established and can be bypassed.
evidence: TemporaryInstanceChecks.BuildOwnedInstanceEnvironment keeps non-product variables; IsProductVariable tests raw prefixes. CheckOwnedInstanceEnvironment does not normalize unknown aliases before accepting them. ScratchQBrainAi sets the owned underscore spelling and starts through OwnedInstanceProcess.
Program.cs adds environment configuration; McpDatabaseConfigurationResolver.ResolveSqliteConnectionString returns a configured connection string before consulting the explicit data-source fallback.

The pinned .NET 10 EnvironmentVariablesConfigurationProvider implementation, lines 65-123 and 145-152, normalizes __ to : and overwrites the normalized dictionary entry. This is a static counterexample from source, not a reviewer-executed product test.

OwnedInstanceEnvironmentTests and OwnedInstanceIsolationContractTests cover the declared prefix forms but have no colon/mixed-separator alias collision row. Passing current TRX therefore does not prove this input class.
Findings.makePass: Normalize configuration-key identity before deciding ownership, remove or reject every inherited alias of a product/database setting, and validate the effective selection before starting the instance. Preserve canonical/legacy and host-prefixed behavior. Add the discriminating contract rows below before the implementation, bind the same rows, and supply the required gate TRX at the resulting code head.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: normalized-configuration-key-ownership
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.statement: Equivalent configuration-key spellings, including colon, double-underscore and mixed separators, cannot change a temporary instance from its explicitly owned database, workspace, marker or address; this holds for either enumeration order and canonical, legacy and host-prefixed forms.

proposedTests.name: OwnedEnvironment_NormalizedAliasesCannotOverrideDatabase
proposedTests.statement: Given explicit inherited and owned maps containing colliding colon, double-underscore and mixed-separator keys in both orders, the effective database remains the owned database and unrelated variables remain intact.

proposedTests.name: StartCheck_RejectsUnownedNormalizedAliases
proposedTests.statement: Given a direct start environment containing an unowned equivalent database key, the check refuses the start before any database access. A wrong implementation that checks only raw prefixes is rejected by the same rows.

Findings.title: Four unit cases still depend on live-clock age comparisons
Findings.defect: The tests manufacture recorded timestamps from the real clock and the called service compares them with another real-clock reading. QueryAsync_TurnStatusInProgressAndStaleOlderThanHours_ReturnsOnlyStaleOpenTurns uses now minus 30 hours and now minus one hour against a live 24-hour cutoff. InitializeAsync_RemovesStaleTemporaryArtifacts sets last-write time to now minus three hours against a live two-hour cutoff. Rule_InProgressTurn_OlderThan48h_UtcClock and Rule_StaleThresholdOverride_BoundedAuthenticatedRecorded seed now minus 49 or ten hours and construct WorkspaceValidationService with TimeProvider.System. A clock change across those margins changes the asserted result. A sufficiently delayed stale-turn query also ages the recent item across the cutoff. These are age decisions, not hang guards.
evidence: All four named methods are present and Passed in both supplied 4739-case unit runs; they have no Integration classification.

SessionLogService computes its stale cutoff using DateTimeOffset.UtcNow. GraphRagService cleanup still uses DateTimeOffset.UtcNow rather than its injected CRUD clock. WorkspaceHygieneG5OverlayTests.CreateService passes TimeProvider.System to a service that already supports an injected clock.

TR-MCP-USECASE-018 AC-006 explicitly requires checked recorded times to come from test-owned scripted inputs and forbids results that change with elapsed time, scheduling or the system clock. The retained sweeps do not establish this for the age comparisons inside the called production code.
Findings.makePass: Use test-owned scripted clocks for the reference time and the compared timestamps, including the called stale-query and artifact-cleanup paths. Preserve all existing assertions. Sweep other age, expiration and staleness comparisons through their production callees, not only assertions that spell out a clock read. Prove the additional contract cases and provide the resulting full gate evidence.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: scripted-recorded-age-boundaries
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.statement: A unit-proved age, expiry or staleness decision uses a supplied scripted reference time and supplied recorded times. Its result is determined by those inputs alone, including immediately before, at and after the threshold, regardless of the system clock or time spent between steps.

proposedTests.name: StaleTurnQuery_UsesScriptedAsOfTime
proposedTests.statement: For fixed recorded turns and a scripted as-of time, only the specified stale in-progress turns are returned at before/at/after boundaries; completed turns stay excluded and no state is closed.

proposedTests.name: ArtifactCleanup_UsesScriptedAgeBoundary
proposedTests.statement: For supplied artifact timestamps and a scripted reference time, cleanup removes exactly the artifacts beyond the age threshold and retains the others.

proposedTests.name: WorkspaceHygiene_UsesScriptedStaleThreshold
proposedTests.statement: Both the default and bounded override thresholds classify fixed turn timestamps against a supplied clock; out-of-range overrides remain rejected. A wrong implementation using the system clock is rejected by the contract.

failList.title: Configuration-key aliases escape temporary-instance isolation
failList.defect: The inherited-environment scrub and start check recognize raw prefixes such as QBrainAi__ and Mcp__, but not equivalent colon-delimited or mixed colon/double-underscore configuration keys. An inherited QBrainAi:Database:Sqlite:ConnectionString survives the scrub and is ignored by the ownership check beside the owned QBrainAi__Database__Sqlite__ConnectionString. The .NET environment provider normalizes double underscores to colons and assigns normalized keys in enumeration order. If the inherited alias is assigned last, it supplies the database connection string. The configured connection string is used before the owned data-source fallback. Consequently the claimed refusal before access to an outside database is not established and can be bypassed.
evidence: TemporaryInstanceChecks.BuildOwnedInstanceEnvironment keeps non-product variables; IsProductVariable tests raw prefixes. CheckOwnedInstanceEnvironment does not normalize unknown aliases before accepting them. ScratchQBrainAi sets the owned underscore spelling and starts through OwnedInstanceProcess.
Program.cs adds environment configuration; McpDatabaseConfigurationResolver.ResolveSqliteConnectionString returns a configured connection string before consulting the explicit data-source fallback.

The pinned .NET 10 EnvironmentVariablesConfigurationProvider implementation, lines 65-123 and 145-152, normalizes __ to : and overwrites the normalized dictionary entry. This is a static counterexample from source, not a reviewer-executed product test.

OwnedInstanceEnvironmentTests and OwnedInstanceIsolationContractTests cover the declared prefix forms but have no colon/mixed-separator alias collision row. Passing current TRX therefore does not prove this input class.
failList.makePass: Normalize configuration-key identity before deciding ownership, remove or reject every inherited alias of a product/database setting, and validate the effective selection before starting the instance. Preserve canonical/legacy and host-prefixed behavior. Add the discriminating contract rows below before the implementation, bind the same rows, and supply the required gate TRX at the resulting code head.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: normalized-configuration-key-ownership
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.statement: Equivalent configuration-key spellings, including colon, double-underscore and mixed separators, cannot change a temporary instance from its explicitly owned database, workspace, marker or address; this holds for either enumeration order and canonical, legacy and host-prefixed forms.

proposedTests.name: OwnedEnvironment_NormalizedAliasesCannotOverrideDatabase
proposedTests.statement: Given explicit inherited and owned maps containing colliding colon, double-underscore and mixed-separator keys in both orders, the effective database remains the owned database and unrelated variables remain intact.

proposedTests.name: StartCheck_RejectsUnownedNormalizedAliases
proposedTests.statement: Given a direct start environment containing an unowned equivalent database key, the check refuses the start before any database access. A wrong implementation that checks only raw prefixes is rejected by the same rows.

failList.title: Four unit cases still depend on live-clock age comparisons
failList.defect: The tests manufacture recorded timestamps from the real clock and the called service compares them with another real-clock reading. QueryAsync_TurnStatusInProgressAndStaleOlderThanHours_ReturnsOnlyStaleOpenTurns uses now minus 30 hours and now minus one hour against a live 24-hour cutoff. InitializeAsync_RemovesStaleTemporaryArtifacts sets last-write time to now minus three hours against a live two-hour cutoff. Rule_InProgressTurn_OlderThan48h_UtcClock and Rule_StaleThresholdOverride_BoundedAuthenticatedRecorded seed now minus 49 or ten hours and construct WorkspaceValidationService with TimeProvider.System. A clock change across those margins changes the asserted result. A sufficiently delayed stale-turn query also ages the recent item across the cutoff. These are age decisions, not hang guards.
evidence: All four named methods are present and Passed in both supplied 4739-case unit runs; they have no Integration classification.

SessionLogService computes its stale cutoff using DateTimeOffset.UtcNow. GraphRagService cleanup still uses DateTimeOffset.UtcNow rather than its injected CRUD clock. WorkspaceHygieneG5OverlayTests.CreateService passes TimeProvider.System to a service that already supports an injected clock.

TR-MCP-USECASE-018 AC-006 explicitly requires checked recorded times to come from test-owned scripted inputs and forbids results that change with elapsed time, scheduling or the system clock. The retained sweeps do not establish this for the age comparisons inside the called production code.
failList.makePass: Use test-owned scripted clocks for the reference time and the compared timestamps, including the called stale-query and artifact-cleanup paths. Preserve all existing assertions. Sweep other age, expiration and staleness comparisons through their production callees, not only assertions that spell out a clock read. Prove the additional contract cases and provide the resulting full gate evidence.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: scripted-recorded-age-boundaries
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.statement: A unit-proved age, expiry or staleness decision uses a supplied scripted reference time and supplied recorded times. Its result is determined by those inputs alone, including immediately before, at and after the threshold, regardless of the system clock or time spent between steps.

proposedTests.name: StaleTurnQuery_UsesScriptedAsOfTime
proposedTests.statement: For fixed recorded turns and a scripted as-of time, only the specified stale in-progress turns are returned at before/at/after boundaries; completed turns stay excluded and no state is closed.

proposedTests.name: ArtifactCleanup_UsesScriptedAgeBoundary

proposedTests.name: WorkspaceHygiene_UsesScriptedStaleThreshold
proposedTests.statement: Both the default and bounded override thresholds classify fixed turn timestamps against a supplied clock; out-of-range overrides remain rejected. A wrong implementation using the system clock is rejected by the contract.
